title: Grateful Dead Live at Saenger Performing Arts Center on 1982-09-09
source: flac16/48kHz; Source Info: Dan Healy's Master Soundboard Cassettes (Sony TC-D5M/TDK MA-R90/Dolby B)> Frank Streeter's 1st generation 1/4 track Reels @ 3.75 ips (Sony TC770/Maxell UD35-90B) > Dat (16-bit/48k); Transfer Info: Dat (Sony PCM-R500)> Tascam DA-3000 (wav 16-bit/48k)> Adobe Audition 3.0 > TLH flac1648; the original version had a duplicate "Space" ("Drums > Space" were 1 track, followed by "Space" again)

ai_review.summary: Soundboard source suffers from fast‑pitch and balance problems, but the show shines with a monster Wheel and a solid Estimated Prophet.
ai_review.review: The Miller/Clugston SBD captures an uneven first set – Jerry muffs Mississippi Half‑Step and the band wrestles into Althea before Bob Weir quits the stage – but the second set recovers spectacularly, delivering a long, “awful good” Wheel and a tight Estimated Prophet jam. Technical flaws (pitch being 2‑4% fast, a brief Space dropout and overall balance issues) limit the listening experience.

ai_rating.rationale: Reviewer gave an overall three‑star rating; musical performance is average with clear highlights, while recording quality is notably poor due to pitch and balance problems.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Pitch runs 2‑4% fast across most tracks, requiring correction; brief dropout at start of Space; overall mix balance needs intervention.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set feels tentative and is cut short by Bob Weir's equipment exit during Althea; second set picks up momentum, delivering strong jams and a memorable Wheel that restores the concert’s energy.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Muffs Mississippi Half-Step, adds extra parts on Franklin's Tower, drops a solo in West L.A. Fadeaway, then moves to rhythm/lead after Weir leaves stage.
band_member_comments.Bob: Leaves the stage early during Althea due to equipment problems, disrupting the first set.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent Mydland steps forward during Althea, taking both rhythm and lead duties.
